prompt: Explain why the length of a vector is the square root of x squared plus y squared.

beats.say: Here is a vector: three steps across, and two steps up.
Drop its shadow onto the axes, and a right triangle appears.
Its length is the long side, so by Pythagoras it is the square root of three squared plus two squared.
That is the square root of thirteen, a little over three and a half.

beats.show: In general, the length of (x, y) is $\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$.
